kind: Runtime observations from a developer dedicated server against a legitimate retail installation, with measurements from retail jamp.exe and the retail multiplayer module; the record accumulated sections through 2026-09-22
installation: legitimate retail Jedi Academy 1.01, read never written
claims: no gameplay, module, wire or rendering claim; module boundary reached and refused by name; later sections report a bot match running with no refused import, which is a milestone and not a compatibility claim
isolation: every run used an isolated fs_homepath in a temporary directory; no client started, no window opened, no input injected
command: fntech3.ded.exe +set fs_basepath "<installation>" +set fs_homepath <temp> +set com_gameProfile jka-mp +set dedicated 1 +set logfile 2 +map mp/ffa1 +quit
build: developer build, -Djka-development=true (later superseded by the 2026-10-11 profile-availability change)

ordinaryBuildAtRecord.result: refused at detection with 'fnTech3 game profile detection failed (the game is recognized, but its engine adapters are not yet complete; see docs/fntech3/COMPATIBILITY.md, evidence: command line)'

startup.automaticDetection: asks for a mode because one installation carries both

module.jka-mp: jampgamex86.dll unpacked into the engine's cache; vmMain found at 20092A10; GAME_INIT called
module.serverinfo: dmflags 0, fraglimit 20, g_gametype 0, mapname mp/ffa1, protocol 26, g_saberLocking 1, gamename basejka
module.gamesLog: base/games.log opened through the engine's filesystem

firstFrontier.message: Jedi Academy game import G_UNLINKENTITY (35) is not served yet: its module boundary is still open. Its arrays are bound.

startup.jka-sp: refuses before loading anything; the module hands the engine a function table nothing reads yet

importService.firstCrash: access violation when the module called back through Raven's import numbers and nothing served them
importService.unservedPolicy: stop with the import's name and number rather than returning an invented answer
importService.G_SET_SHARED_BUFFER: served completely; holds the pointer; imports that would read or write it stay refused

G_G2_CLEANENTATTACHMENTS.initial: doing nothing, held by tests/jka_module_refusal_tests.py failing if another Ghoul2 import was served
G_G2_CLEANENTATTACHMENTS.later: really clears held attachments; the invariant now checks the clearing is real

importService.G_LOCATE_GAME_DATA: binds the module's entity and client arrays to the checked view at Raven's strides; the engine reports its arrays are bound
importService.navigationNo: engine tells the game it loaded no navigation graph; retail installation ships 24 .nav files, one per multiplayer map; a test fails if any other navigation import is served while the decline stands

ghoul2Server.holds: the model, the .gla it names and each bone count; not the pose
ghoul2Server.reuses: the bounded model readers that swept both installations
ghoul2Server.instancePointers: owned by the engine and checked on the way back in; a stale, freed or off-stack address is refused (tests/raven_ghoul2_server_tests.cpp)
ghoul2Server.skins: server skin handle held; file read and surfaces remembered; nothing about drawing
ghoul2Server.instanceCopy: copy owns its models; changing or releasing either leaves the other alone
ghoul2Server.attachments: engine remembers which instance belongs to which entity number; release takes attachments with it
ghoul2Server.bolts: registered by name, a surface first and then a bone; unknown name reports no bolt

entityStateAdapter.check: a record with a distinct value in every one of its 532 bytes round-trips byte for byte
entityStateAdapter.linkAndUnlinkServedByName: Quake III's 34 and 35 are G_BOT_ALLOCATE_CLIENT and G_BOT_FREE_CLIENT; handing Raven's numbers through would free a bot client instead of unlinking an entity

importBoundary.botProfileCorrection: profile said COM_BOT_AI_QUAKE; installation contradicts it; now says what was measured
importBoundary.formerMessage: couldn't load weapons.c, truthfully, for a file the game never had

levelRun.result: the retail multiplayer module runs from GAME_INIT through level spawning and into its frame loop and refuses nothing; holds the level open
levelRun.lastModuleMessage: Unable to save navigations data for map "mp/ffa1" (checksum:-1695889585)
levelRun.navSave: G_NAV_SAVE answers it wrote nothing; the engine will not write a .nav file into a read-only installation
levelRun.navChecksumMatches: the second four bytes of the retail maps/mp/ffa1.nav in assets0.pk3
levelRun.claims: no client connects, no snapshot built, no packet encoded

botConnection.path: module reads botfiles/bots.txt; engine allocates a client slot; userinfo written; goal, move and weapon states allocated out of the bot library; Ghoul2 instance duplicated and attached; skeleton read; bolts registered by name

usercmd.relationToQuake3: Quake III's first twenty-one, then a force power, an inventory item and a general command where Quake III keeps a second weapon and a field of view; the three movement bytes sit one byte later

elementaryActions.reason: Raven inserted an alternate attack and a force power into the middle of Quake III's block; everything after sits two higher

botConnection.inputFrameReadBack: the module's single call site reads action flags at offset 32, once as a byte and once as a word it clears bits in
botConnection.vectorGuard: refused a missing box, which is how a point trace is asked for; now allows the two a trace may leave out, refuses a missing vector elsewhere and names the call and numbers

botPlaysThenRegresses.initialState: bot moved about the level and took items (Item: 0 weapon_disruptor, weapon_thermal, ammo_powercell)
botPlaysThenRegresses.whyItDidNotSurvive: the saber loader was failing for every lightsaber, keeping the game off the branch that asks for a bolt on a saber
botPlaysThenRegresses.afterLoaderFix: bot connects, enters, begins, and is refused G_G2_GETBOLT (587)

playerState.check: a record with a distinct value in every one of its 1552 bytes round-trips

starNamedSkeleton.message: models/weapons2/saber_w.glm: the skeleton it names is not there
starNamedSkeleton.cause: the mesh names *default; a name beginning with a star is not a file
starNamedSkeleton.effect: with sabers loading, the game asked for four more Ghoul2 calls it had never reached

poseMeasurement.engineInstructions: 0x497a23: and ecx, 0xffffff then imul ecx, ecx, 0xe
poseMeasurement.composition: transform applied to the bone's own rest matrix, no hierarchy walk
poseMeasurement.frame: frame = startFrame + ((now - startTime) / 50) * animSpeed; a Ghoul2 frame is fifty milliseconds
poseMeasurement.blend: element by element across the whole matrix, not a quaternion slerp
poseMeasurement.supersession: see 2026-09-22-jka-pose.json, which records that these pose inferences were later corrected by live engine-query comparison

finalBotRun.log: ClientConnect: 0; PLCONNECT; PLENTER; ClientBegin: 0; Item: 0 weapon_disruptor; Item: 0 weapon_thermal
finalBotRun.jediOutcast: reaches the same on ffa_bespin with two bots, out of the same shared store (see 2026-09-22-jk2-records.md)

openItems: G_NAV_LOAD answers it loaded nothing; the navigation graph stays empty and all twenty-three navigation imports answer out of it; six do nothing and say why in their source; the next step would be reading a .nav file
the module never calls G_NAV_INIT or G_NAV_FREE
an earlier passage reports a saber_w.glm skeleton warning for models/weapons2/saber/saber_w.glm as unresolved; the star-named explanation above resolves the related models/weapons2/saber_w.glm case
the configstring calls and the entity-token reader may or may not be exercised against the module; not counted
no map drawn, no packet encoded or decoded, protocol 26 remains a registered number
one installation, one edition, one platform
